_comment: CANON spec of the QSC-9 (Quantum Singularity Core) drive — the Ascendant's engine. Single source of truth so Ada and the game reference the same parts. 'kind' = visible (rendered in the engine_room scene, hotbox-able) | instrument (a readout/console) | external (outside the hull) | conceptual (referenced, not distinctly rendered). 'where' = where it sits in the current engine_room image, for tracing hotspots.
principle: A charged micro black hole suspended in an electromagnetic containment trap. Fed mass to sustain output; its emission (Hawking/accretion radiation) is caught by a reflector and directed as thrust, with a tap for ship power. The hard problem is heat: in vacuum it can only be shed by radiation.

components.name: Singularity Core
components.where: the bright glowing center of the reactor tower
components.function: The charged micro black hole itself. Never seen directly — only its accretion glow and gravitational lensing. Converts fed mass to energy.

components.name: Electromagnetic Containment Trap (the bottle)
components.where: the banded rings of the tower and the radial coil ring at its base
components.function: Holds the charged singularity suspended so it never touches matter or drifts. The single most critical safety system aboard.

components.name: Containment Vessel
components.function: The armored chamber shell around the core and its field.

components.name: Containment Aperture
components.where: the glowing vertical slot at the tower's midline
components.function: The shielded port the instruments read the core through — where the spectro-pyrometer looks.

components.name: Radiation Reflector / Collector
components.where: within the core assembly (not distinctly rendered)
components.function: Parabolic mirror that catches the core's emission and directs it as thrust, tapping some for ship power.

components.name: Mass/Charge Feed Injector
components.function: Feeds reaction mass to sustain output and tops up the core's charge so the trap keeps its grip.

components.name: Coolant Loops & Pumps
components.where: the curved pipe loops on the sides of the tower, and the overhead conduits
components.function: Carry heat off the containment. The inlet/outlet temperature difference (delta-T) is the number Ada watches most.

components.name: Heat Exchangers
components.function: Hand heat from the coolant to the radiators.

components.name: Radiator Panels
components.where: outside the hull — visible through the viewports only when deployed
components.function: Deploy to shed heat to space. Deploying them exposes them to micrometeorites — a real tradeoff.

components.name: Spectro-Pyrometer
components.where: a dedicated drive console (assign one of the side consoles)
components.function: Reads core temperature from the emission spectrum (blackbody peak / Wien's law). The gauge the player first clicks without understanding.

components.name: RTD / Thermocouple Array
components.where: contact sensors across containment, coolant, radiators (read on the console)
components.function: Direct-contact temperatures for everything you can physically touch.

components.name: Drive Control Console
components.where: the side consoles with blue screens (left and right of the tower)
components.function: Where Ada — and eventually the player — reads margins and sets the burn / radiator schedule.

components.name: Core-Ejection System
components.where: a guarded control on the console / a hatch beneath the tower
components.function: Jettisons the singularity if containment fails. A loose black hole means the ship is gone.

components.name: Backup Containment Power
components.where: a reserve feed to the trap
components.function: Redundant power to the bottle. If the trap loses power, the core is free.

thermal_problem: The core runs above its rated thermal envelope. The spectro-pyrometer gives core temp; the coolant delta-T shows how fast heat is being carried off; radiator output shows how fast it's being shed to space. The duty-cycle question: schedule drive burns and radiator deployment to hold the core in the green without adding days to the voyage or over-exposing the radiators.
